NOTE:  PUBLIC PARTICIPATION INFORMATION
  Pursuant to the  Governor's  Executive  Order  N-29-20,  City  Council  Members  may  participate  via
  teleconference.

  Public Participation:
  In accordance with Executive Order N-29-20 and guidance from the California Department of Public
  Health on limitations on gatherings and social distancing requirements, members of the public are
  requested not to attend the meeting in person and instead utilize the following methods of remote public
  participation:

  - City Council meetings are live-streamed on PVP-TV Channel 35 (Cox) and Channel 39 (Verizon) and on
  the City’s website at www.rhe.city.

  - Public comment will be accepted by email to LaurenP@RollingHillsEstatesCA.gov prior to the meeting
  and during the meeting, prior to the close of public comment on an item, and read into the record during
  public comment.

  Agenda reports and other disclosable public records relating to each Open Session agenda item are
  available on the City's website under City Council Meeting agendas at www.RollingHillsEstatesCA.gov.
  Meetings are live broadcast on the City's website and a recording is available for viewing after each
  meeting. Meetings are also broadcast on PVP-TV Channel 35 (Cox) and Channel 39 (Verizon).

MINUTES
  CITY COUNCIL MEETING
  MARCH 24, 2020

A regular meeting of the City Council of the City of Rolling Hills Estates was called to
order by MAYOR SCHMITZ at 7:02 p.m. via teleconference, pursuant to the Governor’s
Executive Order N-29-20.

2.  SALUTE TO THE FLAG

3.  ROLL CALL

City Council Members Present:  Huff, Mitchell, Schmitz, Zerunyan and Zuckerman

  “COVID-19”.

  CITY MANAGER’S PROCLAMATION OF A LOCAL EMERGENCY REGARDING

A.  ADOPTION OF AN URGENCY ORDINANCE OF THE CITY OF ROLLING HILLS
  ESTATES AMENDING AND RESTATING CHAPTER 17.56, OF THE ROLLING
  HILLS ESTATES MUNICIPAL CODE PERTAINING TO THE REGULATION OF
  ACCESSORY DWELLING UNITS, TO TAKE EFFECT IMMEDIATELY AFTER
  ADOPTION; AND INTRODUCTION OF AN ORDINANCE OF THE CITY OF
  ROLLING HILLS ESTATES AMENDING AND RESTATING CHAPTER 17.56, OF
  THE CITY OF ROLLING HILLS ESTATES MUNICIPAL CODE PERTAINING TO
  THE REGULATION OF ACCESSORY DWELLING UNITS

  Recommendation: That the City Council 1) open the Public Hearing; 2) receive any
  public testimony; 3) close the Public Hearing; 4) waive further reading; 5) adopt
  Urgency Ordinance No. 728; 6) introduce on first reading Regular Ordinance No.
  729; and 7) continue the Public Hearing for a second reading and adoption of Regular
  Ordinance No. 729, to the City Council meeting of May 12, 2020.

  Planning Manager Naughton provided a staff report (as per the agenda material).

  Public comment was invited via email before and during the public hearing, as
  noticed on the Agenda and on the City’s website and social media platforms.

  MAYOR PRO TEM ZUCKERMAN confirmed that if a primary dwelling is connected
  to a sanitary sewer, then a proposed ADU must also be connect to the sewer.

CITY COUNCIL MINUTES  3
MARCH 24, 2020
   MAYOR PRO TEM ZUCKERMAN asked if there was a possibility to incentivize
  the use of solar panels and disincentivize the use of gas in ADUs. Planning
  Manager Naughton explained that Solar cannot be a requirement, but they City
  could provide education and incentives to encourage the use of solar energy, and
  to research any applicable grants.

  COUNCIL MEMBER MITCHELL confirmed that the uniform Building Code
  requirements adopted by the City would all be required and must be complied with.

  City Attorney Davis addressed comments received as public correspondence from
  the Californians for Homeownership.

  COUNCIL MEMBER MITCHELL moved, seconded by, COUNCIL MEMBER
  HUFF TO OPEN THE PUBLIC HEARING.

  There being no objection, MAYOR SCHMITZ so ordered.

  City Clerk Pettit reported that no public testimony was received.

  COUNCIL MEMBER MITCHELL moved, seconded by, COUNCIL MEMBER
  HUFF TO APPROVE AS FOLLOWS BY THE FOLLOWING ROLL CALL VOTE:

  1) WAIVE FURTHER READING; AND 4) ADOPT URGENCY ORDINANCE
  NO. 728.

  AYES:  Huff, Mitchell, Schmitz, Zerunyan, Zuckerman
  ABSENT:  None

  COUNCIL MEMBER MITCHELL moved, seconded by, COUNCIL MEMBER
  HUFF TO APPROVE AS FOLLOWS BY THE FOLLOWING ROLL CALL VOTE:

  1) INTRODUCE ON FIRST READING REGULAR ORDINANCE NO. 729;
  AND 2) CONTINUE THE PUBLIC HEARING FOR A SECOND READING
  AND ADOPTION OF REGULAR ORDINANCE NO. 729, TO THE CITY
  COUNCIL MEETING OF MAY 12, 2020.

  AYES:  Huff, Mitchell, Schmitz, Zerunyan, Zuckerman
  ABSENT:  None

B.  INTRODUCTION OF AN ORDINANCE OF CITY OF ROLLING HILLS ESTATES
  ADOPTING A NEW CHAPTER 17.78 OF THE ROLLING HILLS ESTATES
  MUNICIPAL CODE PERTAINING TO THE PERMITTING OF SPECIAL EVENTS
  AND REPEALING MUNICIPAL CODE CHAPTER 5.64 REGARDING
  TEMPORARY USE PERMITS

  Recommendation: This item is continued until May 12, 2020.

  CONTINUED UNTIL MAY 12, 2020.

9.  NEW BUSINESS

NONE.

10.  OLD BUSINESS

NONE.

10.  CITY ATTORNEY ITEMS

CITY COUNCIL MINUTES  4
MARCH 24, 2020
 City Attorney Davis commented on the meeting procedures being used in accordance with
the Governor’s Executive order as stated at the opening of the meeting. The newest
Executive Order now allows for concurrent emergency briefings regarding COVID-19
without any noticing or agenda.

11.  CITY COUNCIL/REGIONAL COMMITTEE REPORTS

MAYOR PRO TEM ZUCKERMAN reported on the Vector Control meeting he attended this
month, where he learned that the Director will be retiring.

MAYOR PRO TEM ZUCKERMAN also reported on the Clean Power Alliance offices at
WeWork downtown, which is now closed after a visitor tested positive for COVID-19.
Everyone is currently working sufficiently in the cloud, and the CPA will be moving into new
offices within the next couple of months.

12.  MAYOR AND COUNCIL ITEMS

COUNCIL MEMBER ZERUNYAN reported that California Contract Cities unanimously
canceled the Annual Municipal Seminar in May in light of the current pandemic.

COUNCIL MEMBER MITCHELL reported on the cancellation of the Southern California
Association of Governments Regional Conference & General Assembly in May due to the
pandemic. She also reported that the California Association of Councils of Government
Regional Leadership Forum in April has been canceled. Lastly, the South Bay Cities Council
of Governments (SBCCOG) Annual General Assembly in March has been postponed.

COUNCIL MEMBER HUFF reported that the SBCCOG meeting for March has been
canceled, but that future meetings will likely happen via teleconference.

MAYOR PRO TEM ZUCKERMAN reported on the last SBCCOG meeting he attended with
the cities of Rolling Hills and Rancho Palos Verdes regarding dues.

MAYOR PRO TEM ZUCKERMAN asked staff to look into how many viewers tuned into the
live-stream City Council meeting. He also asked staff to look into how long before CalPERS
increases our contribution rate to mitigate the impaired portfolio due to the COVID-19
pandemic. City Manager Grammar noted that staff is monitoring the situation very closely.

MAYOR SCHMITZ reported that the Sanitation Districts meeting was moved to
teleconferencing and has been rescheduled. The Peninsula Mayor’s lunches have also
moved to virtual meetings.

MAYOR SCHMITZ thanked City staff for working tirelessly during this difficult time and
stated that our City has been communicating very effectively to the community with our well-
coordinated message, and that other local cities are praising and emulating what we are
doing.

13.  CLOSED SESSION

NONE.

14.  ADJOURNMENT

At 8:05 p.m. MAYOR SCHMITZ adjourned the City Council meeting. The next City
Council meeting will be held on Tuesday, April 14, 2020 at 7:00 pm.

Submitted by,  Approved by,

Lauren Pettit,  Greg Grammer
City Clerk  City Manager

CITY COUNCIL MINUTES  5
MARCH 24, 2020
